searchText: <@!425274498732916736> re https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-2315-simple-subroutines-for-the-evm-analysis/4229/41?u=holiman . I don't understand the 'shadow map' implementation. Is it limited to handing `1024` byte long subroutines? Or rather: how do you encode a 24K long subroutine into six bits? Also, we don't have to distinguish betweej JUMPDEST?BEGINSUB in the map, since we can check that in the code before we even consult the analysis. So one bit should be sufficient, leaving 7 bits instead of 6 I think I got the gist of the leb encoding now.. I think I'll try out the shadowmap alternative, with 7-bit encoding instead of 6 True, but that requires two lookups in different arrays. On the other hand we are jumping there anyway... I made an implementation. The speed difference of the analysis is definitely noticeable (a factor of 2-3), and that's _with_ the cap. If we don't have a cap on code, things become slower still (e.g then the LEB-encoder needs to handle larger numbers). So I would really _not_ want to roll that out without the cap https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/pull/21161
